source: Toprank Review Academy (TRA) Nursing Module – Complete Handout

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How should the client be positioned for an abdominal exam?
questions.rationale: Flexing the knees relaxes the abdominal muscles during the exam.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: During abdominal examination, it is important to flex the knees to relax the abdominal muscles

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Where does the nurse stand to palpate the thyroid?
options: At the foot of the bed
questions.rationale: The nurse stands behind the client to palpate the neck for lymph nodes or thyroid enlargement.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: the nurse stands behind the client

questions.subject: NP I
questions.stem: A male nurse examines a female client. What ethical safeguard is needed?
questions.rationale: A female nurse must be present when a male examines a female client.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Physical Exam (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: female nurse must be in attendance to ensure that the procedure is done in ethical manner

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Foul-smelling perspiration is called:
questions.rationale: Bromhidrosis is foul-smelling sweat; hyperhidrosis is excessive sweating.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Care (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Bromhidrosis isfoul-smelling perspiration

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A flat, colored spot smaller than 1 cm, like a freckle, is a:
questions.rationale: A macule is flat, circumscribed, under 1 cm; a patch is larger.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 23)
questions.quote: Macule — flat, circumscribed area of color with no elevation; <1cm (Freckles)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A raised, fluid-filled lesion under 1 cm, as in chickenpox, is a:
questions.rationale: A vesicle is a small serous blister; a bulla is larger; a pustule has pus.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Vesicle — circumscribed elevation serous fluid or blood <1cm blister. chicken pox)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A linear scratch mark exposing the dermis is a(n):
questions.rationale: An excoriation is a superficial linear or hollowed-out area exposing the dermis, such as a scratch.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Skin Lesions (PDF p. 24)
questions.quote: Excoriation – superficial linear or hallowed out rust area exposing dermis.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: During a bed bath, how are the eyes cleaned?
questions.rationale: Eyes are cleaned with water only, inner to outer canthus, using a separate mitt corner for each eye.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bed Bath (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Cleanse eyes with water only, wiping from inner to outer cantus.

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: How are the arms and legs washed during a bed bath?
options: Long firm strokes, distal to proximal
questions.rationale: Long, firm strokes from distal to proximal promote venous return.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Bed Bath (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: using long, firm strokes from distal to proximal areas

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Non-blanchable redness of intact skin over the sacrum is which pressure injury stage?
questions.rationale: Stage I is non-blanchable erythema of intact skin.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pressure Ulcer (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Stage I — non-blanchable erythema of intact skin

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: A pressure ulcer with exposed muscle and bone is stage:
questions.rationale: Stage IV involves full-thickness loss with damage to muscle, bone, or supporting structures.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Pressure Ulcer (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Stage IV — full-thickness skin loss with extensive destruction

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which measure helps prevent pressure ulcers?
options: Keep head of bed at 30° or less
questions.rationale: Keeping the HOB at 30° or less reduces shear. Avoid massaging bony areas and powders; turn every 2 hours or more often.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Prevention of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Reduce shearing force by elevating the bed not more than 30 degrees

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which solution is AVOIDED when cleaning a pressure ulcer?
questions.rationale: Ulcers are cleansed gently with alcohol-free cleanser; hydrogen peroxide damages tissue.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Treatment of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Do not use hydrogen peroxide

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Which debridement uses enzyme agents such as collagenase?
questions.rationale: Chemical debridement uses collagenase; sharp uses a scalpel; autolytic uses moisture-retaining dressings.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Treatment of Pressure Ulcers (PDF p. 25)
questions.quote: Chemical debridement uses collagenase enzyme agents

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: A client disagrees with the dose of a medicine. What should the nurse do?
questions.rationale: The nurse rechecks the medication order if the client disagrees with the dose.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Medication Administration (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: re-check the medication order if the client disagrees with the dose.

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which is one of the Ten Rights of medication administration?
questions.rationale: The Ten Rights include right drug, dose, client, route, time, documentation, approach, right to know, right to refuse, and drug history.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Ten Rights (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Right to refuse

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An unexpected drug response unique to one client is a(n):
questions.rationale: Idiosyncratic effects are unexpected and individual; toxic effects come from overdose or buildup.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Medication Action (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Idiosyncratic effects — unexpected and maybe individual to a client

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An order to give a drug 'immediately, once' is a:
questions.rationale: A stat order is a single dose given immediately.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Types of Order (PDF p. 26)
questions.quote: Stat - An order for a single dose of medication to be given immediately

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which tablet must NEVER be crushed?
questions.rationale: Enteric-coated and sustained-release tablets are never crushed.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Route (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: Never crush enteric coated or sustained release tablets

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: What should the nurse do before pouring a suspension?
questions.rationale: A suspension is water-based with settled particles; the bottle is shaken before use.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Oral Drug Forms (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: Suspension – water-based liquid medication, shake the bottle before use

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Why should a sublingual tablet not be swallowed?
questions.rationale: Sublingual drugs dissolve and absorb rapidly under the tongue; if swallowed, gastric juice may inactivate them.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Sublingual Route (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: If swallowed, may be inactivated by the gastric juice

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: At what angle is an intradermal injection given?
questions.rationale: Intradermal injections use a 25–27 gauge needle at 10–15° bevel up to form a wheal, without massage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Intradermal Injection (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: Needle at 10 to 15 degree angle level up

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: Why does the nurse avoid massaging the site after insulin injection?
questions.rationale: Massaging an insulin site speeds absorption; sites are rotated to prevent tissue damage.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Subcutaneous Injection (PDF p. 27)
questions.quote: For insulin injection, do not massage to prevent rapid absorption

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the Well Child (Neonate to Adolescent)
questions.stem: Which is the IM site of choice for infants 1 year and younger?
questions.rationale: The vastus lateralis is the IM site of choice for infants 1 year and younger.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IM Injection (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: Vastus lateralis is the site of choice for IM injections for infants 1 year and younger

questions.subject: NP II
questions.topic: Care of the At-Risk and Sick Child
questions.stem: Using Clark's rule, what is the dose for a 30-lb child if the adult dose is 500 mg?
questions.rationale: Clark's rule: weight in lb ÷ 150 × adult dose = 30/150 × 500 = 100 mg.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Calculating Dosages (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: (Clark’s rule)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How is a glass ampule opened safely?
questions.rationale: Using gauze or an opener, the top is snapped by bending it toward you so it breaks away from yourself and others.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Ampules (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: break off the top by bending it toward you to ensure the ampule is broken away from yourself

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which needle is used to draw medicine from a glass ampule?
questions.rationale: A filter needle removes glass particles and is replaced with a regular needle before injecting.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Ampules (PDF p. 28)
questions.quote: Replace the filter needle with a regular needle

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: How should a vial of reconstituted medicine be mixed?
questions.rationale: Mix by rotating the vial between the palms, not by shaking.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Preparing from Vials (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: Mix the solution if necessary by rotating the vial between palms of the hands, not by shaking

questions.subject: NP IV
questions.stem: When mixing regular and NPH insulin, which is drawn up FIRST?
questions.rationale: Air is injected into NPH, then regular, and regular insulin is always withdrawn first to avoid contaminating it.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Mixing Insulins (PDF p. 29)
questions.quote: always withdraw regular insulin first

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which IV solution is hypotonic?
questions.rationale: 0.45% and 0.33% NaCl are hypotonic; NS and LR are isotonic; D5NS is hypertonic.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Solutions (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: 0.45% NaCl (half normal saline)

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which IV solution can help treat metabolic acidosis?
questions.rationale: Lactate is metabolized in the liver to bicarbonate, so LR is alkalinizing.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Solutions (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Lactated ringer’s is an alkalinizing solution that maybe given to treat metabolic acidosis

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: Which vein should be chosen FIRST for a peripheral IV?
options: A distal vein of the non-dominant arm
A vein over the elbow joint
A vein in an injured arm
questions.rationale: Use distal veins first, on the non-dominant arm, that are soft, full, and splinted by bone; avoid flexion areas and injured limbs.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, Vein Selection (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Use distal veins of the arms first

questions.subject: NP III
questions.stem: An IV solution looks cloudy. What does this mean?
questions.rationale: Solutions must be clear; cloudiness is evidence of contamination.
questions.source: TRA Nursing Module, IV Equipment (PDF p. 30)
questions.quote: Cloudiness is evidence that the solution is already contaminated
